liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Scarlet Begonias, Fire On The Mountain, and Morning Dew are cited as all-time best versions; The transition into Fire On The Mountain is the main reason to keep the show [32][35]
- **Lazy Lightning** (1 review): The transition into Supplication is loved, specifically when Bobby sings a high note [31]
- **Dancin' In The Streets** (1 review): The performance is criticized for having too much goofy pseudo disco feel [35]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): The performance of this song is described as giving listeners chills [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-05-08.sbd.cantor.sacks.266.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 205 min; rated 4.72/5 by 36 [1]
- **gd77-05-08.sbd.hicks.4982.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 180 min; rated 4.64/5 by 300 [2]. Said about its sound: The soundboard recording is called impeccable, surpassing most official Dead live releases; This is identified as the best sounding soundboard recording of the Dead; The recording is a freshly remastered Betty Board with audience splices [2][26][27]
- **gd1977-05-08.mtx.seamons.97274.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 177 min; rated 4/5 by 18 [6]. Said about its sound: Instrument pickup is great, but vocals are lower than in Moore's copy [6]
- **gd1977-05-08.111493.mtx.seamons.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 177 min; rated 4.63/5 by 35 [3]

## Around the show

- Phil's bass performance is highlighted as one of the best aspects of the show [31]
- There were a few pauses, including a tape flip after Supplication [6]
- The setlist for the first set began with New Minglewood Blues [37]
- The reviewer argues May 1977 was the best tour, allowing lossless comparisons to older tapes [25]
- Every second set song is claimed to be a top ten version [26]
- The first set is unremarkable except for the closer, which is terrific [30]
- The show is overshadowed by performances from May 7, June 9, and September 3, 1977 [30]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-05-08.sbd.cantor.sacks.266.shnf**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Darrin Sacks; source: WBOTB Source -- 7" two track BBD reel encoded w/ DBX-1 noise reduction @ 7 1/2 ips > Sony PCM501ES @ 44.055 kHz. Sony PCM501ES analog out > DBX-1 decoder >… [1]. Also: Audience splices used a Panasonic boom box with condenser mics, transferred to CD [1]
- **gd77-05-08.sbd.hicks.4982.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Maizner; transferred by Rob Eaton; source: Matrix (see notes) [2]. Also: No soundboard exists; the recording is from audience tapes that sound like a soundboard; Betty Board master Nagra reels were transferred by Rob Eaton using Sony PCM gear [2][34]
- **gd1977-05-08.mtx.seamons.97274.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [6]. Also: Handheld Shure 57s were placed ten feet from stage, feeding a TC152 recorder [6]
- **gd1977-05-08.111493.mtx.seamons.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (SHN & FLAC>AIFF>Final Cut>WAV>FLAC); this source fixes a flaw in d1t08 from source ID 97274 [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jay Maybrey: [Celebrate the legendary Grateful Dead show at Barton Hall, performed 48 years ago today](https://nysmusic.com/2025/05/08/celebrate-the-legendary-grateful-dead-show-at-barton-hall-performed-43-years-ago-today/) [38]
- Poster by arizjones.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead, Barton Hall, Cornell University, Ithaca, New York, 5-08-1977](https://arizjones.blogspot.com/2015/06/grateful-dead-barton-hall-cornell.html) [39]
- Poster by Mabrey: [1977 Grateful Dead Cornell Concert Poster](https://www.icollector.com/1977-Grateful-Dead-Cornell-Concert-Poster_i8463417) [40]
- Fan art by blackmuddyblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1977-05-08 - Barton Hall, Cornell University, Ithaca NY (Get Shown The Light, Part II)](https://blackmuddyblog.blogspot.com/2017/05/grateful-dead-1977-05-08-barton-hall.html) [41]
- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1977-05-08 Barton Hall Cornell University Ithaca, NY](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2017/02/grateful-dead-1978-05-08-barton-hall.html) [42]
- Poster by Luke Z. Fenchel: [Revisiting The Grateful Dead's 1977 Barton Hall show](https://www.ithaca.com/news/local_news/revisiting-the-grateful-deads-1977-barton-hall-show/article_9bc4474d-7463-5140-9b7c-7df7bb1b0264.html) [43]

The reviewer argues May 1977 was the best tour, allowing lossless comparisons to older tapes
The soundboard recording is called impeccable, surpassing most official Dead live releases
Every second set song is claimed to be a top ten version
This is identified as the best sounding soundboard recording of the Dead
The first set is unremarkable except for the closer, which is terrific
The show is overshadowed by performances from May 7, June 9, and September 3, 1977
The transition into Supplication is loved, specifically when Bobby sings a high note
Phil's bass performance is highlighted as one of the best aspects of the show
Scarlet Begonias, Fire On The Mountain, and Morning Dew are cited as all-time best versions
No soundboard exists; the recording is from audience tapes that sound like a soundboard
The performance is criticized for having too much goofy pseudo disco feel
The transition into Fire On The Mountain is the main reason to keep the show
Audience splices used a Panasonic boom box with condenser mics, transferred to CD
Betty Board master Nagra reels were transferred by Rob Eaton using Sony PCM gear
The recording is a freshly remastered Betty Board with audience splices
Handheld Shure 57s were placed ten feet from stage, feeding a TC152 recorder
Instrument pickup is great, but vocals are lower than in Moore's copy
There were a few pauses, including a tape flip after Supplication
